title: Twins’ Joe Ryan surrenders franchise-record 6 home runs in return from All-Star break
content:
CLEVELAND — After one of the worst starts of his career, one in which he established a franchise record, Joe Ryan didn’t have many answers.

Making his first start since the All-Star break, the Minnesota Twins right-hander lasted only four innings in Monday night’s series opener, surrendering a career-worst six home runs to the light-hitting Cleveland Guardians. Ryan allowed eight earned runs and a career-high 10 hits as the Guardians pounded the Twins 13-4 at Progressive Field.

“Still trying to figure it out,” Ryan said. “It seemed like they tried a very accurate game plan. Guys that haven’t hit fastballs this year are hitting them over their head, out. … They put really good swings on the ball and did the damage they did. I don’t want to take credit away from that. But yeah, definitely sucks. Not the way you want to start a series.”

The outing marked the first time Ryan pitched for the Twins since he struck out two in a scoreless inning for the American League during Tuesday’s All-Star Game in Philadelphia, the second All-Star appearance of his career.

Before the start, Ryan was 6-5 with a 2.85 ERA and only 10 home runs allowed in 110 1/3 innings this season.

Brayan Rocchio started Cleveland’s long ball party with a two-run homer, which came with two outs in the first inning. Rhys Hoskins followed with a solo shot, the second time all season Cleveland hit back-to-back homers.

“We’ve seen him pitch at 92-93 and throw seven innings and be effective, and we’ve seen him throw 95s and 96s,” Twins manager Derek Shelton said. “He wasn’t sharp with anything. It’s just one of those days where he didn’t have his good stuff.”

And the Guardians, who entered Monday tied for 27th among 30 teams in baseball with 94 homers, were at their best and only getting started.

Petey Halpin hit a two-run blast in the second inning for the first home run of his MLB career. Two batters later, Travis Bazzana hit Cleveland’s fourth round-tripper.

Hoskins hit his second of the night, and the team’s fifth, to start the third inning, and Halpin, who entered the game with a .471 OPS in 71 plate appearances, belted the Guardians’ sixth homer to lead off the fourth.

Ryan had twice allowed five home runs in a start before Monday night. In an outing at San Diego on July 29, 2022, Ryan served up five long balls and a career-worst 10 earned runs. He also yielded five round-trippers in a start at Atlanta on June 27, 2023.

“Just kind of a weird week,” Ryan said. “Didn’t really get to throw a bullpen. Trying to figure some stuff out physically and where we’re at, syncing things up. It’s just one of those where I was trying to figure it out pregame, thought I was feeling really good, and then you go out there, and it’s not going the right way. It’s definitely frustrating.”

It marked the third straight poor outing from a Twins starting pitcher. Taj Bradley surrendered five earned runs in a 6-2 loss to the Chicago Cubs on Saturday, and Zebby Matthews allowed 10 runs (eight earned) in a 10-1 blowout loss to Chicago on Sunday.
